skills.name: adr-workflow
skills.summary: Establish and maintain Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) in software repositories.

skills.name: analyze-cohesion
skills.summary: Analyze the cohesion of a class, module, file, or package and recommend split, merge, or leave — classify it on the cohesion scale and compute LCOM.
skills.compatibility: The bundled LCOM script needs Python 3.8+. It analyzes Python (precise, via AST), R, and Bash (heuristic) sources. The reasoning workflow is language-agnostic.

skills.name: analyze-coupling
skills.summary: Measure or judge how coupled or brittle a codebase is.
skills.compatibility: Works on any codebase. The bundled script is stdlib-only Python 3.8+. Dependency-graph extraction uses whatever tool fits the ecosystem (examples below for Python, JS/TS, Java, .NET, Go).

skills.name: architecture-pattern-advisor
skills.summary: Use when choosing the architecture of a repository — topology (monolith, modular monolith, microservices, serverless) or code organization (layered, by-domain, hexagonal, clean/onion).

skills.name: balanced-coupling
skills.summary: Judge whether a specific dependency between two components is acceptable.
skills.compatibility: Works on any codebase or design document. The bundled checker script is stdlib-only Python 3.8+. No dependency-graph tooling required — the assessment is qualitative, per relationship.

skills.name: c4-modeling
skills.summary: Draft a C4 model of a software system with the user and render it as Mermaid diagrams.
skills.compatibility: No dependencies — Mermaid renders natively on GitHub, GitLab, VS Code, and most Markdown tools. Optionally C4-PlantUML for publication-grade output when PlantUML (Java) or a Kroki server is available.

skills.name: codebase-design
skills.summary: Shared vocabulary and workflow for designing deep modules.

skills.name: communication-analysis
skills.summary: Analyze or rewrite a message, feedback, or conversation with Schulz von Thun's four-sides model and Rogers-style active listening.

skills.name: ddd-advisor
skills.summary: Advise on Domain-Driven Design strategically (subdomain classification, context-mapping) and tactically (choosing an implementation pattern, then modeling Entities, Value Objects, Aggregates).

skills.name: ddd-conventions
skills.summary: Correctness and design conventions for writing or reviewing code in a Domain-Driven Design codebase — aggregates, value objects, domain events, event sourcing, bounded-context integration.

skills.name: fitness-functions
skills.summary: Design and implement architecture fitness functions.

skills.name: fowler-refactoring-catalog
skills.summary: Look up Martin Fowler's refactoring catalog to name the exact technique for a code smell and get its atomic mechanics.

skills.name: grilling
skills.summary: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design.

skills.name: guideline-distillation
skills.summary: Distill messy source documents (style guides, ADRs, RFCs, wikis, linter configs) into lean, machine-actionable rules files (CONVENTIONS.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) for coding agents.

skills.name: handoff
skills.summary: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.

skills.name: hypertrophy-training
skills.summary: Summarizes evidence-based hypertrophy-training programming and auto-regulation with precise stop criteria.

skills.name: llm-application-engineering
skills.summary: Guide the engineering of a foundation-model application across three linked decisions.

skills.name: logical-component-design
skills.summary: Forward, generative decomposition of a NEW system or feature into named logical components — Richards & Ford's iterative identify-and-refine cycle.

skills.name: microservices-design
skills.summary: Apply distilled microservices design conventions from Newman's *Building Microservices* when designing or reviewing how services interact.

skills.name: ml-project-lifecycle
skills.summary: Guide a machine learning project from problem framing through model selection to production deployment.

skills.name: natural-planning
skills.summary: Walk a project through GTD's Natural Planning Model (purpose -> outcome -> brainstorm -> organize -> next actions) to turn a vague, stuck, or overwhelming project into concrete physical next actions.

skills.name: problem-first-explanation
skills.summary: Output-form skill for technical explanations — forces every explanation to start with the concrete problem the concept solves, before the abstract solution or implementation.

skills.name: prototype
skills.summary: Build a throwaway prototype to flesh out a design — a runnable terminal app for state/business-logic questions, or several radically different UI variations toggleable from one route.

skills.name: r-error-constructors
skills.summary: Design custom condition/error constructors for R packages the tidyverse/rlang way.
skills.compatibility: R packages using rlang for condition signaling and testthat for testing; assumes tidyverse-style package conventions (roxygen2 `@export`, `NAMESPACE`-managed S3 methods).

skills.name: r-package-dev
skills.summary: R package internals — package-private state and persistence, loading/attaching, lifecycle hooks and API deprecation, and interface-focused testing with fixtures.
skills.compatibility: Requires R 4.0+ for tools::R_user_dir() (use rappdirs fallback on older R). No network required.

skills.name: refactoring-checklist
skills.summary: Decide whether, when, and how to refactor a spotted code smell — prioritize the backlog, gate on coverage and change size, and refactor safely in reversible small steps.

skills.name: repo-status
skills.summary: Generate a standup / status update from recent development activity — yesterday/today/blockers, turning rough notes or connected-tool activity into a shareable update.

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.summary: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance.
skills.compatibility: Claude Code, Claude.ai, Cowork, Codex CLI, OpenCode (trigger evals need the claude CLI; codex trigger support is experimental)

skills.name: sql-schema-design
skills.summary: Apply module-encapsulation thinking to SQL schema design and query patterns.

skills.name: stakeholder-update
skills.summary: Generate a stakeholder update tailored to audience and cadence — weekly/monthly leadership status, launch announcement, risk escalation, or exec/engineering/customer versions of the same progress.

skills.name: stepdown-rule
skills.summary: Write, refactor, or review functions using the stepdown rule.

skills.name: tdd
skills.summary: Test-driven development.

skills.name: to-issues
skills.summary: Break a plan, spec, or PRD into independently-grabbable issues on the project issue tracker using tracer-bullet vertical slices.

skills.name: uncertainty-management
skills.summary: Manage risky, hard-to-predict changes by decomposing them into small validated steps, checkpointing before each one, and rolling back on trouble.

skills.name: worry-management
skills.summary: Use when someone brings a specific distressing worry, anxious rumination, or recurring "what if" and explicitly wants help thinking it through.

skills.name: zettelkasten-value-hierarchy
skills.summary: Classify personal knowledge-base notes on an 8-level value hierarchy (Principle > System > Workflow > Automated Tool > Template > Checklist > Tool > Snippet).
